text: Why do some people work every single day, and still stay broke?
Three men live by the same river. Each one owns a single fishing line. Nothing else.
The first man catches one fish a day. He eats it that night. Every night. Same fish. Same hunger.
The second man works longer. He catches two. He eats one, and dries the other for bad days.
The third man stops fishing. For a whole week, he just sits there, tying knots.
By day five, he's starving. So he goes to the second man.
Lend me ten dried fish, and I'll pay you back twenty.
On day eight, he throws his net. One throw.
Soon he has two nets. Then five. Too many to pull alone.
So he offers the first man a job. Three fish a day. Three times what he used to catch.
One sold his time. One saved it. One built something that catches fish while he sleeps.
The fish were never the difference. The net was.
